lesson_title: The Buried Saucer: SA's Platinum Superpower
hook_text: Most of the world's platinum sits in one buried saucer — and it's ours.
clip_script: Deep under the bushveld lies a gigantic, ancient saucer of once-molten rock — the Bushveld Igneous Complex. As it cooled, its minerals settled into flat layers, the way cooling soup settles, and a few of those layers — the Merensky Reef, the UG2 — are stuffed with platinum. The saucer's rim breaks the surface in three arcs, and that is where the mines line up, with Rustenburg the capital of platinum country. Almost every petrol and diesel car on earth carries a little of this metal in its exhaust.
visual_style: 3D cutaway of a vast layered saucer under the veld, arcs glowing where mines line up, zooming from headgear at Rustenburg to a car's exhaust pipe.
pacing: Slow reveal of the saucer, quick snap to the world market, strong close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — four lucky cards, the hindering factors, and how to spot a mine on any map.
